scenario: AITA for no longer cooking for my roommate because he dumps condiments on everything? | Because I love cooking and (at the risk of sounding arrogant) I'm pretty good at it, I've always volunteered to be in charge of dinner when dividing up chores with roommates. I'm **not** saying my food is perfect. There are a lot of things I'm trying to improve on. But I learned to cook from two professional chefs, I don't have a lot of typical issues like under-seasoning or over-cooking food, and even when I'm living with other people that are also good at cooking I'm usually asked to prepare food 3+ nights a week. Even if I'm not incredible, I at least know what I'm doing. Since this comes up later: we have a shared food budget for staples/basic ingredients (pasta, broth, canned vegetables, flour, sugar, spices, etc). Half the time we'll split the cost of meat and fresh ingredients, half the time I pay for them myself and and accept booze, snacks (another roommate is a phenomenal baker), chores, or favors as payment. The problem is, one of my newer roommates puts condiments on everything he eats. I'm not just talking about things like hamburgers, chicken wings, mac and cheese, or anything else that normally gets condiments. I've seen him put ketchup, mayo, hot sauce, A1, or barbeque sauce on chili, steak, alfredo, fried rice, curry, pizza, red sauce, gumbo, ribs that are already covered in BBQ sauce... you get the idea. And that would be fine, I guess, but he A) does it without even trying the food first and B) completely smothers the food with them. I've tried to talk to him about this. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even stuff he says he likes prepared the way he says he likes it gets the same treatment. I've asked him to at least try the food first but he refuses. I've explained that it bothers me when I put effort into a meal and he treats it the same way he treats fast food and microwave dinners, but he said it was still being eaten so it didn't matter. I finally got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. He's been complaining to my other two roommates because his monthly expenses have gone way up (he doesn't cook at all, so he either eats out or buys prepackage meals) and saying that I'm being petty and over dramatic. My baking roommate says she agrees with my decision and the other roommate doesn't care, he just wants mealtimes to be less dramatic. AITA? I think I did plenty to meet him halfway.

I love cooking and I'm pretty good at it, so I usually take charge of cooking dinner when we divide up chores with our roommates. I'm not saying my food is perfect, but I've learned from professional chefs and I know what I'm doing. Even when I'm living with other good cooks, I'm usually asked to prepare food a few nights a week. Now, the issue is with one of my newer roommates. He puts condiments on everything he eats, not just the usual stuff like burgers or fries, but even on things like chili, steak, alfredo, fried rice, curry, pizza, red sauce, gumbo, ribs that are already covered in BBQ sauce... you get the idea. And it's not just a little bit; he completely smthers the food with them. He does this without even trying the food first, which is frustrating because I put effort into the meal. I tried talking to him about this. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even when I prepare things the way he says he likes them, he still adds all the condiments. I asked him to at least try the food first, but he refuses. I explained that it bothers me when I put effort into a meal and he treats it the same way he treats fast food or microwaved dinners, but he said it didn't matter because he was still eating it. Finally, I got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. He's been complaining to my other two roommates, saying that his monthly expenses have gone up because he doesn't cook at all and now he has to eat out or buy prepackaged meals. He thinks I'm being petty and overdramatic. My baking roommate agrees with my decision, and the other roommate doesn't care, he just wants meal times to be less dramatic. So, is this AITA (Ask a Internet Therapist/Advisor)? I think I did plenty to meet him halfway. Alright, so to figure out if I'm right or wrong, I need to consider a few things. First, is it reasonable to expect that someone won't add condiments to a meal I've prepared? I mean, people have different tastes, and adding condiments is pretty common. But in this case, he's adding them to everything, even when it's not necessary, and without trying the food first. That seems excessive. Second, did I handle the situation appropriately? I tried talking to him, offering to make his favorite meals, and explaining how it bothers me. When that didn't work, I decided to stop cooking for him. That seems like a reasonable response, but maybe I could have communicated my feelings more clearly or found a compromise. Third, is it fair for him to complain to the other roommates about his increased expenses? He doesn't cook, so if I'm not cooking for him, he has to find other ways to eat, which might cost him more. But is it fair for him to blame me for his financial situation? Or is he just upset because he's not getting the meals he's used to? Also, how do the other roommates feel about this? My baking roommate agrees with me, and the other roommate doesn't care, he just wants meal times to be less dramatic. So, it seems like at least one roommate supports me, which is good. But maybe I should consider if there's a way to compromise. For example, could I agree to cook for him on certain nights if he agrees not to add condiments, or at least try the food first? Or could we split the cooking responsibilities more evenly so that he doesn't feel the burden when I'm not cooking for him? Another thing to consider is the shared food budget. We have a shared budget for staples and basics, and half the time we split the cost of meat and fresh ingredients, and half the time I pay for them myself and accept other things as payment. So, if I'm not cooking for him, does that mean he's not contributing to the shared budget? Or is he still expected to contribute? Also, how does this affect the overall dynamic in the house? If I'm not cooking for him, and he's complaining to the other roommates, it could create tension. Maybe I should talk to the other roommates together to find a solution that works for everyone. In summary, I think I did what I could to handle the situation, but maybe there's a better way to communicate or find a compromise. It's important to consider the feelings of all roommates and find a solution that works for everyone, not just me or him.
